tagline: Over the swing bridge to an opera house without operas.
intro: Route 82 comes over the Connecticut on the East Haddam Bridge, 889 feet of riveted steel with a swing span at the east end, and lands beside the Goodspeed Opera House. From there Route 149 turns north up Main Street, along the big river and then the Moodus River, for a little over two miles.

This is East Haddam's long, thin village. It began as two 18th-century landings, Upper and Lower, that traded with the East and West Indies until the railroad was laid up the other bank. The steep ground just east of them kept them from spreading that way, so they grew together into one long village.

moments.title: East Haddam Swing Bridge
moments.text: It opened on Flag Day 1913 with a 17-gun salute and a Model T parade, and took over from the ferries that had worked the river since the 1690s.

moments.title: Goodspeed Opera House
moments.text: The stage is on the top two floors, reached by a scenery shaft and a winch, and the story goes that the wind once carried a piece of Annie's set into the river.

moments.title: East Haddam Historic District
moments.text: Route 149 runs the length of the old landings, past the town's civic buildings, a cemetery, and monuments to Nathan Hale and General Joseph Spencer.
